name: Tamar Matossian
title: Neurodevelopmental Specialist
photoAlt: Tamar Matossian, founder and director of The Hummingbird Nest
bio:
Tamar is a Neurodevelopmental Specialist, specializing in the DIR Floortime® approach with {years} Years experience working with the Neurodiverse population. She is the founder and director of The Hummingbird Nest and author of the book: [What’s Autism](https://www.amazon.com/dp/069285620X).

Tamar holds a CL-1 Profectum Certification for DIR Floortime®, a Speech Language Pathology Assistant License and UCLA PEERS® Certification for [The Social Club](https://www.thesocialclubkids.com) social learning group program. Thus, she uses a multidisciplinary approach in all her sessions to ensure maximum development.

Tamar conducts staff training for schools and child facilities, as well as providing parent coaching services.

name: Juliana Reyes
photoAlt: Juliana Reyes, DIR Floortime developmental specialist
bio:
Juliana’s approach as a DIR Floortime® Developmental Specialist at The Hummingbird Nest is grounded in relationship-based, developmental, and play-focused strategies. Her work emphasizes sensory regulation, body awareness, and bottom-up nervous system support as foundational to engagement and learning.

Drawing from her background as a Registered Yoga Teacher, Juliana integrates movement and co-regulation strategies into DIR Floortime® and Social Club sessions to help children feel safe and regulated in their bodies. Juliana has led children to emotional regulation, social engagement, and meaningful connection by meeting each child at their developmental level and building trusting relationships with families.

Juliana is a graduate of the University of California, Santa Cruz, where she earned her bachelor’s degree in Psychology and Latin American and Latino Studies.

name: Selena Santana
photoAlt: Selena Santana, DIR Floortime developmental specialist
bio:
Selena Santana is a DIR Floortime® Developmental Specialist at The Hummingbird Nest with a background in psychology and cognitive science, as well as experience supporting children with autism. Her approach is rooted in relationship-based, developmental, and play-centered principles that prioritize connection as the foundation for growth.

Selena focuses on supporting social development and independence in daily routines, helping children build the skills needed for meaningful participation in everyday life. She incorporates sensory awareness and co-regulation strategies into her sessions to promote engagement, flexibility, and confidence. By following each child’s lead and honoring their individual developmental profile, Selena fosters authentic connection while partnering closely with families to support ongoing progress.
